title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1966-05-19
lineage: MR > DAT > FM Broadcast > CDR > SHN

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy early‑1966 soundboard capture with excellent vintage clarity, highlighted by a scorching Rider and rare Mindbender/ Cream Puff War performances.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers a raw yet surprisingly clear glimpse of the Dead in their garage‑blues phase.  The set is packed with standout moments – a fiery Rider, the only known live Tastebud (aka “Come Back Baby”), blistering Mindbender and a historic Cream Puff War – all presented on a soundboard source that sounds remarkably good for a tape over three decades old.  While a few quirks (a slightly slow pitch and a missing intro to BIODTL) are noted, the overall experience is consistently praised as a must‑hear early show.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews (≈90 %) award 4–5 stars, praising both the performance and the surprisingly good sound quality; only a handful note minor flaws, leading to a strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced for a 1960s tape; reviewers cite crisp vintage sound, occasional pitch/slowness issue and missing intro to BIODTL, but overall the mix is listenable with front‑of‑stage drums and Pigpen prominent.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A loose, high‑energy early‑Dead set that blends blues covers with nascent originals; the pacing is relentless and dance‑able, moving from gritty blues numbers to rare psychedelic moments without losing momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for scorching guitar licks and blistering solos (especially on Rider and Mindbender).
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as “on fire” with energetic, sweet blues bass; occasional mud‑dy bottom end noted but overall strong.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ solo on Good Lovin' highlighted; no specific comments about a dedicated keyboardist.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy’s drumming lauded as fantastic, particularly on Viola Lee Blues and Cream Puff War; bass drum sound singled out as impressive.
